implementation_notes: The base action maps cleanly onto Django's class-based views: View.dispatch is the template method every request crosses, AccessMixin subclasses (LoginRequiredMixin, PermissionRequiredMixin, UserPassesTestMixin) supply the standard checks, and a project base view composes them so each concrete view declares only its business logic. Overriding dispatch() in the base is the idiomatic place for shared steps the mixins do not cover, such as session validation, tenant resolution or audit stamping.
pitfalls: Mixins run in MRO order and each may return a response on failure; combining them carelessly changes which check runs first, so pin the order in the base class.
A dispatch() override must call super().dispatch(...) or the view never executes; an early return that was meant as a check silently skips the handler.
login_required semantics differ between the decorator (redirect) and the mixin (403 for authenticated but unauthorized users); align them with the error contract.

variants.name: ASGI/WSGI security middleware wrapping the application
variants.implementation_notes: Where the shared sequence must cover an entire ASGI or WSGI application regardless of routing, middleware is the honest realization: a wrapper around the app performs identity, session and audit handling before passing the request inward, so function views and class views get identical protection without a class hierarchy. It replaces the base handler entirely; use it when the checks are site-wide or must also cover non-view routes (health, admin, static).
pitfalls: Middleware order is LIFO: the last added middleware runs first, so security middleware must be added after logging and before routing for a predictable sequence.
BaseHTTPMiddleware buffers or streams responses differently from pure ASGI middleware; test streaming and background-task paths.
